title: CollectionRun
description: What one collection run did: which slate it operated on, which collectors were invoked, and how each fared. This record exists to answer one question that is otherwise unanswerable — why does this match carry no score from this model? Without it, a source that was down for a week is indistinguishable from a source that had nothing to say.

run_id.description: Identifies this execution. Distinct from slate_id: the same slate collected twice produces two runs.

slate_id.description: The slate this run operated on. Collected data is only interpretable alongside it.

completed_at.description: Absent while the run is in flight.

collectors.description: One entry per registered collector considered for this run, including those not invoked.

entity_kind.description: What this collector keys its output by, which determines how the platform joins it onto matches.

outcome.description: `succeeded` means the source was reached and its answer is trusted, including an answer of 'nothing for this entity'. `failed` means the collector could not determine whether data exists — transient, worth retrying, and NOT the same as absence. `not_invoked` means no active model declared anything this collector provides, so it was correctly never called.

reason.description: Why the collector failed. Required in practice when outcome is `failed`; an unexplained failure is barely better than a silent one.

entities_with_data.description: Entities the collector returned values for. Meaningful only when outcome is `succeeded`.

entities_without_data.description: Entities the collector was asked about and legitimately had nothing for. This is coverage, not failure — the number a model's skip reasons should be read against.

provides.description: Leaf paths this collector claimed at registration, recorded so a run stays interpretable after a path changes producer.
